claims.text: The as-cast FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy will have higher tensile strength than traditional alloys.
The as-cast FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy will have greater ductility than traditional alloys.
The predicted mechanical-property improvements arise from compositional synergy among Fe, Ni, Cr, and Mn.
The material is to be evaluated in its as-cast state.
Tensile testing can be used to evaluate the mechanical properties of the FeNiCrMn alloy.
Microstructural analysis can be used alongside mechanical testing.
The high-entropy composition produces a unique microstructure.
The microstructure produced by the high-entropy composition promotes solid-solution strengthening.
The microstructure produced by the high-entropy composition promotes grain refinement.
Combining multiple principal elements produces a complex microstructure in FeNiCrMn.
The complex microstructure enhances dislocation movement.
The complex microstructure impedes fracture propagation.
The FeNiCrMn alloy will exhibit an approximately 10–20% increase in tensile strength relative to conventional alloys.
The exact tensile-strength and ductility improvements may vary with processing conditions and testing methods.

contradictions.description: The mediator invokes solid-solution strengthening, which ordinarily depends on resistance to dislocation motion, while the mechanism states that the microstructure enhances dislocation movement. The distinction between impeded motion for strength and facilitated plasticity for ductility is not explained.
